Детальніша інформація про компанію на сайті http://eknis.net/ Шукаємо інженера, який у складі команди буде займатись розгортанням, супроводом та розробкою інтеграційних рішень та SCADA-систем для об'єктів енергетики: підстанцій, диспетчерських центрів, об'єктів генерації (СЕС / ВЕС), BESS та мікрогрідів. Також ми створюємо кастомні інтеграційні рішення для взаємодії АСКТП з іншими інформаційними системами. Написання скриптів автоматизації: обробка даних, парсинг файлів і логів, генерація звітів. Аналіз взаємодії компонентів та сервісів ПЗ, розуміння його внутрішньої структури, робота з технічною документацією. Підготовка технічної документації, взаємодія з вендорами і замовниками. Бази даних (MS SQL, PostgreSQL) на рівні впевненого користувача: запити, оптимізація, реплікація, базове адміністрування. Скриптинг та автоматизація засобами PowerShell. Розуміння принципів резервування, моніторингу, журналювання, діагностики збоїв. Англійська на рівні технічної переписки з вендорами. Join our team of Manitoba's best as we continue to build a company that champions safety, supports innovation, and delivers on our commitment to customer service - while actively fostering a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace reflective of the communities we serve. Great Benefits Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package. Defined-benefit pension plan for long-term financial security. Enjoy a work schedule that typically provides every second Monday off (subject to location and operational requirements), supporting a balanced approach to work, family life and community. Position Overview: We are seeking a permanent Network Specialist to join our Control Centre Technology Systems Department in Winnipeg, Manitoba. Responsibilities: Working as a support specialist for Operational Technology (IT/OT) network systems and associated infrastructure (Networking, Firewalls, Load balancers, and Multifactor Authentication systems), provide technical support for network related deployment, and implementation of the EMS, and Gas environments. Participate in the EMS Infrastructure patch management programs and malicious code prevention in accordance with compliance Standards. Complete the day-to-day patching of critical EMS systems. Maintain, and troubleshoot the EMS system, network and associated Operational Technology systems, on a day to day basis, as part of the Infrastructure support team. This may be in conjunction with consultants or vendor representatives. Maintain procedures to ensure the day-to-day reliability and availability of EMS applications, subsystems and related interfaces. This includes developing and executing action plans to resolve system performance deficiencies. Additionally, responsible as the primary Subject Matter Expert (SME) for one or more technologies or processes. Procurement of networking hardware/software as required. Perform and analyze network packet captures. Ability to troubleshoot network problems using network analysis tools. Work with end users and other technical groups to resolve system problems when necessary. Provide 24-hour on call support as part of the EMS Infrastructure on call rotation. Keep abreast of Information Technology advances and methods used to maintain and enhance EMS and OT systems. Respond to system emergencies at any time. Qualifications: A two year Diploma in Computer Programming or Electronic or Computer Technology from an institute of recognized standing and a minimum of five years related experience in the field of information/computer technology. Demonstrated ability in the implementation, maintenance, problem detection and resolution in the following areas: - Networking - Firewalls - Local Balancers - MFA Authentication Systems - Network Monitoring Tools Experience with data centre infrastructure (cooling, racking, UPS). Demonstrated understanding of change management procedures. Understanding of governance, compliance, and security standards such as NIST or NERC CIP. Familiarity with container tools such as Docker or Kubernetes. Familiarity with automation platforms such as Ansible, Puppet, or Terraform. Demonstrated knowledge of scripting or programming language (PowerShell, Bash, or Python). Ability to solve complex problems during periods of high stress. Ability to interpret technical material quickly and concisely. Continuously update and maintain technical knowledge in keeping with the changing technology. Physically capable of performing all the duties of the position. Dependable with mature judgement. Ability to work anytime during a twenty four hour period to provide system availability. Willingness to work long and unusual hours and travel both in and out of province as required. Reside within the headquarters zone. Possess a valid Province of Manitoba Driver's Licence with appropriate classification. Must have completed Standards of Conduct training, or be willing to complete within two weeks of start date. Must obtain and maintain a current Personnel Risk Assessment and a "Clear" security rating in accordance with Manitoba Hydro policy P513. Salary Range Starting salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. The range for the classification is $41.26-$57.11 Hourly, $79,060.02-$109,437.90 Annually. Apply Now! Ready to join a team that energizes Manitoba and puts safety, innovation, and inclusion at the heart of everything we do? Visit www.hydro.mb.ca/careers to learn more about this position and to apply online. Application deadline: NOVEMBER 17, 2026. We appreciate your interest in Manitoba Hydro and thank all applicants. Only those selected for the next stage of the selection process will be contacted. If you require accommodations during the recruitment process or need this posting in an accessible format, please let us know - we're committed to a barrier-free experience for all candidates.

You will apply deep subject matter expertise spanning long-haul optical transport, fiber plant design, and ILA critical infrastructure to cross-functional initiatives that shape how Meta's backbone network evolves to meet the demands of billions of users worldwide. This is a high-impact, high-autonomy role for a senior engineer who thrives on solving complex, large-scale network challenges across the full infrastructure stack. review_candidates.title: Digital Infrastructure Engineer - AI Infrastructure and Strategic Technologies - based in Luxembourg
review_candidates.description: This position is based at our Luxembourg headquarters and requires regular office presence. The EIB offers you the opportunity to live and work in a truly international and multi-cultural environment. We also offer relocation support. The EIB, the European Union's bank , is seeking to recruit for its Projects Directorate (PJ) - Innovation and Competitiveness Department (INCO) - Digital Infrastructure Division (DIGIINFRA), at its headquarters in Luxembourg, a Digital Infrastructure Engineer* - AI Infrastructure and Strategic Technologies. Internal benchmark role: Sector Engineer This is a full-time position at grade 5. Panel interviews are foreseen for November 2026. If you are passionate about the infrastructure powering artificial intelligence and Europe’s strategic technologies, this role offers the opportunity to shape high-impact investments at the intersection of engineering, finance and public policy. You will assess complex projects across AI-ready data centres, high-performance computing, semiconductors, quantum technologies and advanced connectivity, helping strengthen Europe’s digital competitiveness, resilience and technological sovereignty. Purpose The Project Directorate’s (PJ) mission is to provide independent advice to the EIB’s decision makers on the sector policy to be followed and on the quality of investment projects to be financed, advising promoters on the design, preparation and implementation of their projects as well as monitoring the implementation of the ongoing investment projects. To accomplish its role, PJ is mainly staffed with sector experts (Engineers, Economists, Environmental, Climate and Social experts, Procurement experts), who work together in multi-disciplinary project teams, and in a close contact with the other EIB operational services. The Digital Infrastructure Division (DIGIINFRA), part of the Innovation and Competitiveness Department (INCO) of PJ, covers digital infrastructure and strategic technologies, including data centres, high-performance computing, semiconductor value chains, quantum technologies and advanced telecommunications networks. The Division supports the Bank’s strategy for innovation, digitalisation and resilience, including its priorities on Digitalisation and technological innovation and Security and defence. The successful candidate will focus on projects across the AI infrastructure value chain in the EU and in other countries where the Bank operates. The Digital Infrastructure Engineer will assess, within multidisciplinary teams, the strategic alignment, technical soundness, financial viability, resilience, security and sustainability of digital infrastructure investments. You will review technical documentation, prepare appraisal reports and other decision-making material, and monitor approved projects through implementation and completion. You will also contribute to sector studies, policy and methodology work, market intelligence and the identification of new financing opportunities. You will monitor developments across technology, markets and public policy, translate them into practical insights for internal stakeholders, and help develop external cooperation with the European Commission, international financial institutions, specialised institutes and industry partners. You will be required to travel to project locations within and outside the EU, normally for short trips of up to one week depending on the project location. Operating Network Reporting to the Head of the Digital Infrastructure Division, you will work autonomously while collaborating closely with engineers, economists, environmental, climate, social and procurement experts across PJ and with colleagues in Lending, Legal and Risk. You will build strong working relationships with project promoters, private-sector leaders, public authorities, EU institutions, international bodies, specialised institutes and other financial institutions, and represent the EIB at selected sector events and high-level project meetings. Accountabilities As a Digital Infrastructure Engineer, you will help shape and evaluate investments in the technologies underpinning Europe’s AI ambitions. You will combine engineering judgement, investment analysis and strategic insight to support sound financing decisions and deliver resilient, secure and sustainable infrastructure. What You'll Be Doing Appraise strategic infrastructure investments: Assess projects across AI-ready data centres and compute infrastructure, high-performance computing, semiconductor value chains, quantum technologies and advanced telecommunications networks. Deliver robust technical due diligence: Evaluate strategic alignment, technical soundness, , implementation readiness, operational performance, financial viability, resilience, security and sustainability, documenting conclusions in clear appraisal reports. Monitor delivery and results: Follow project implementation, assess completion and undertake further monitoring where required. Shape sector knowledge and policy: Prepare sector, policy and methodology papers and produce concise briefings and updates for internal stakeholders. Track emerging technologies and markets: Interpret technological, market and regulatory developments and share relevant insights across the organisation. Identify financing opportunities: Work with colleagues across the Bank to identify investments that support European competitiveness, resilience and technological sovereignty. Build high-value partnerships: Develop cooperation with EU institutions, international bodies, specialised institutes and financial institutions, and represent the EIB at selected forums and events. Contribute flexibly across priorities: Support other sectors and participate in priority initiatives across the Division, Department, Directorate and Bank. Qualifications University degree, (minimum bachelor’s degree) or equivalent professional qualification, preferably in engineering, computer science, telecommunications, electrical engineering, data centre engineering, semiconductor engineering, physics, applied sciences or a related discipline. At least 5 years (ideally 10 years) of recent and relevant professional experience in digital infrastructure project development, engineering or investment assessment. Preference may be given to candidates working at senior level and managing complex tasks or projects. Proven experience assessing complex infrastructure projects across feasibility, design, implementation and operation. A strong interest in, and at least a basic understanding of, two or more of the following: AI-optimised data centres, hyperscale or colocation infrastructure; HPC, GPU/accelerator clusters and cloud infrastructure; semiconductor manufacturing, advanced packaging and related supply chains; advanced telecom networks, fibre backbones, data centre interconnect and 5G/6G infrastructure, quantum computing or related technologies. Very good knowledge of the digital infrastructure sector, including global and EU policy and market trends, together with an understanding of infrastructure investment economics such as economic and financial rates of return and net present value. – Potential screening question Excellent analytical and strategic-thinking skills, with a practical, results-oriented approach to problem solving. Sound judgement and resilience in complex, sensitive and time-critical assignments, and experience working in diverse international environments. Excellent knowledge of English and/or a good command of French (*). Knowledge of other EU languages would be an asset. Excellent knowledge of German would be an asset. Competencies Find Out More About EIB Core Behavioural Skills Here To find out more about our eligibility criteria click here (***) Unless stated explicitly as a required qualification, a good command of French is not a pre-requisite for hire. As both English and French are however official working languages of the EIB, proficiency in both languages is a pre-requisite for your future career development. Any language clause in your contract must be fulfilled in order for you to be eligible for a promotion (either via the annual appraisal cycle or via an internal selection process). Proficiency is understood to mean the attainment of level 5 of the Inter Institutional language courses, corresponding to B1.2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFRL). The Bank offers appropriate training support. We hire and value talent with unique characteristics, creating a work environment where they can be themselves. We believe that Diversity, Equity and Inclusion makes us a performing and innovative organisation. We encourage all suitably qualified and eligible candidates to apply regardless of their gender identity/expression, age, racial, ethnic and cultural background, religion and beliefs, sexual orientation, disability or neurodiversity. If you require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process due to a disability, neurodivergence, or a chronic health condition, please contact the EIB Recruitment team Jobs@eib.org who will manage your request appropriately. By applying for this position, you acknowledge the importance of maintaining the security and integrity of the Information of the EIB Group. In case of selection for the position you agree to comply with all measures (policies, controls, document classification and management) implemented by the EIB Group to prevent unauthorised disclosure of any information or any damage to the EIB Group reputation. This is an open campaign to consecutively fill open positions. The campaign will remain open until position is filled. Applications will be reviewed in order of receipt.
